## Problem

The completion-verifier close precheck (`_check_work_landed` -> `_referencing_commits` -> `commit_impact.referencing_commits`) walks all code history and resolves every commit's `rebar-ticket:` trailer via `resolve_ticket_id`. When those trailers are aliases, the resolver ran a fresh full-store alias scan (`os.listdir(tracker)` plus a per-ticket CREATE/SNAPSHOT JSON read) for EACH distinct alias -- O(distinct_aliases x store). On the production-scale store (5300+ ticket dirs) a single close hung 70+ minutes at high CPU.

## Approach

Add `_ids.build_alias_index` (one store pass building `{alias -> [dir names]}`) and `_ids._effective_alias_for_dir` (extracted from `_scan_alias`, behavior-preserving). Add an optional `alias_index` parameter to `resolve_ticket_id`; when provided, the alias branch does an in-memory lookup instead of a fresh scan. Build the index once in `commit_impact.referencing_commits` and thread it into each per-ref resolve. Re-export `build_alias_index` from `_engine_support.resolver`. Single-id callers are untouched (the param is optional).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `referencing_commits` builds the alias index once (a single `os.listdir(tracker)` pass) and threads it into `resolve_ticket_id`, so the number of full tracker-root scans does NOT grow with the number of distinct alias trailers in history.
- [x] Correctness is unchanged: the same commits are credited to the same tickets, and every id form (full / short / alias / Jira / prefix) resolves identically to per-call scanning, including ambiguous-alias -> None.
- [x] `resolve_ticket_id`'s existing single-id callers are unaffected (the `alias_index` parameter is optional and defaults to per-call scanning).

## Testing

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py` proves the bounded-scan contract (RED before the fix: N distinct aliases -> N scans; GREEN after: 1 scan) and the indexed-vs-per-call parity including the ambiguous-alias case.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] Verified empirically on the real store: `referencing_commits` for a real ticket drops from 70+ minutes to seconds (checked: measured 4.6s).
